notes: EVERY THRESHOLD IN THIS FILE IS AN UNVERIFIED PLACEHOLDER. The values are plausible for southern Lower Michigan and are here so the model can be exercised and tested; not one of them has been traced to a published source.

Spec open question 4: minimum viable acreage is contested and varies by operator, market, and equipment. An indefensible threshold discredits the whole tool, so no figure here should reach a landowner until it has been checked against MSU Extension enterprise budgets and reviewed by Extension or Conservation District staff.
Until a figure is checked, leave its citation status at unverified-placeholder. The model reports that status in every brief; downgrading it silently is the failure mode this file exists to prevent.
Advisors who disagree with a figure should override it (see applyOverride) rather than edit this file, so the disagreement is recorded against the brief.

citation.source: Working assumption pending MSU Extension crop enterprise budgets
citation.note: Acreage floor is a stand-in for the point below which owning or hiring modern equipment stops penciling. Check against custom-rate work, which lowers it substantially.

citation.source: Working assumption pending MSU Extension forage budgets
citation.note: Hay tolerates small and awkward fields better than row crop; the binding constraint is usually equipment access, not acreage.

citation.source: Working assumption pending MSU Extension grazing and livestock budgets
citation.note: Stocking rate, not acreage, is the real constraint. Water that fails in August is the most common reason a grazing plan collapses.

citation.source: Working assumption pending MSU Extension tree-fruit budgets
citation.note: Air drainage and frost pockets matter more than the figures modelled here and are not represented at all. Site elevation relative to surroundings is the missing variable.

citation.source: Working assumption pending MSU Extension vegetable budgets
citation.note: Market access, labour, and irrigation capital dominate the acreage question. This threshold describes the land only.

citation.source: Working assumption pending Michigan DNR forest management and MSU Extension guidance
citation.note: NCCPI rates commodity cropping and does not describe forest productivity; site index would, and is not modelled. Acreage floor reflects the size at which a harvest attracts a buyer.

citation.source: Working assumption pending NRCS conservation practice standards and MSU Extension guidance
citation.note: Agroforestry covers practices with very different land requirements. Treating them as one enterprise is a simplification that should be revisited before this reaches an advisor.
